implementation.scopeBoundary: Only Search evidence recipe tests and the owning repository's Search evidence cookbook changed, plus this scope's evidence. The public Search schema, SQL constructor metadata, evaluator, sibling repositories, package versions and publication state were not changed.
implementation.recipes: Location-only projections retain scalar occurrence coordinates; short-snippet projections retain exact MatchText; bounded context and expansion use the existing internal SearchContextOptions/SearchMatch evidence seam and are explicitly not advertised as a new SQL constructor.

The separate ownership review approved the recipe boundaries, trust handling, complete no-match guidance and provenance; exact commands, tool versions, source/artifact hashes and the unique trailer-bearing completion commit are retained.
Recipe tests preserve occurrence cardinality and coordinates under compact/context projections, verify Unicode-safe byte truncation, and retain exact zero-count semantics.
The documented SQL examples use the existing two-argument Search constructors; the location, snippet and counts forms compile and run, and the Search warnings-as-errors build passed.

Bounded context output honors the UTF-8 per-window budget, avoids unpaired surrogates, and expansion uses the existing source-identity checked seam; no pooled memory or lifecycle implementation changed in this scope.

knownLimitations: MatchText is not governed by the context byte budget; callers must choose a short or otherwise bounded literal/pattern when using it as a display snippet.
Bounded context remains an internal execution seam; the current SQL constructors expose no context options and SQL exposes no terminal summary row.
A repository-wide negative answer requires complete counts and eligible-path accounting; an empty occurrence relation alone is not sufficient.
Expansion detects source changes with identity checks but does not claim an atomic snapshot of a live filesystem.
